cells.tense: Right now you are the one turning, and the turning is yours to make.
cells.ask: Show up for one thing on purpose this week, finish it, then leave the next thing alone until it arrives on its own.
cells.core:
You meet what shows up as it shows up. Not bracing for it and not behind it. Something new arrives and you are already turned toward it, in the first second of it instead of standing three seconds ahead of yourself.

That first second is the whole thing. A conversation starts, news lands, a day opens, and you are there for it without rehearsal and without having decided how it will go. When this is holding, you finish what is here and stay open to what is next, and the two do not fight. Keep the finisher's hand on what closes and the receiving hand open.
cells.sheetLine: You meet what arrives as it arrives, and you know you're doing it.
cells.place: the place where you become what you already are

cells.tense: You are already living in what has not happened yet, bracing for a version of events you have not met.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are rehearsing and put it down for today. Finish one thing that is actually here, all the way to done, then stop.
cells.core:
You get carried instead of steering. A moment arrives and you are already past it, decided about how the day is going to go, so the day obliges and you did not get to meet it. The cause stays out there, in the room or the timing or the other person, anywhere but in your own hand.

When this is holding, the same day reads differently. The next thing is just next, not a verdict, and you get to be there for its first second. Bracing skips that second. The way back is not to stop what is moving. It is to finish the one thing you are standing in and let that be everything you do today.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that has already closed behind you.
cells.ask: Do one small ordinary thing that only exists in the world when you do it — a meal, a list, a message sent — and let it count as today.
cells.core:
You have gone quiet at the entry. The turning keeps happening in the world and you have stepped off it, watching from the side and calling that the wiser place. Turning away can look like peace from the outside and feel like a room you do not have to be in.

When this is holding, the small thing gets done and the moment lands without a story attached to either one. If showing up to the ordinary thing feels like more than you have, that is information, not a verdict. Charge the small act, not the arrival feeling. Start with something that does not need you to be ready.
cells.sheetLine: You stepped off the turning, and the turning kept going without you.

cells.tense: The pen is already moving while you are calling the writing someone else's.
cells.ask: Before you react to the next thing that happens today, name out loud whose day this is. Then make one choice from that, not from the reaction.
cells.core:
You arrive at the result and are surprised by it. A week takes a shape, an ending takes a shape, and the cause of the shape sits somewhere out there, in the timing or the other person. The surprise is honest. The missing part is yours: the turning happens because someone turns it.

When this is holding, you know which moment you are in because you put yourself there. Look back through one recent day and find one moment you decided. It does not have to be big. Finding it is the whole thing. The turning is quiet enough to miss, which is why it runs unclaimed. Claim the next one before it lands.
cells.sheetLine: The wheel is turning, and you've been calling that someone else's hand.
cells.place: the place where you become what you already are

The reader could reasonably say the pulling is just how life works and not their pattern at all. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line where the wheel turns on its own and the read gets mystical — I have kept the turning as the person's own act.
